Interesting Dining Experience
Feb 2020
The food here was really nice. It's a bit pricey but it's still really good.
They have some authentic Vietnamese food here and that's great.
They also have some really nice Vegetarian meals (you just need to make sure when ordering, because most of the time the vegetarian food can still have some seafood in it, so just be sure to ask, and if you struggle with the language barrier use Google translate)
Was quite an experience here. This is also where we were properly introduced to Durian (which was used to spice or flavour one of the meals), unfortunately it was quite overpowering for us, and personally didn't like it. But that does not meal the food wasn't good, it's just a personal opinion on the flavour of the fruit.
The rice in the clay pots are really nice and are served in generous portions. And the vegetarian curry is really good!

Nit picky pricing
Jun 2019 • Family
We had dinner and ordered the chicken, prawns, vegetables, spring rolls, and fried fish. We also ordered guava juice and a fruit smoothie. The quality of the food (ie freshness, cooking method) was good, but the overall flavor across the board was bland. The restaurant itself had a classy, elegant ambiance, though it was mostly empty. 

What really turned me off, though, was that they charged for the moist towelettes, which should either be included in the price of food, or they should offer a ‘standard’ napkin free of charge. Of course, it didn’t show up until we paid the bill, and therefore had no option to refuse the towelettes. This type of hidden pricing is just plain dishonest. The cost was very little, but it’s wrong on principle.

reviews.review_text:
jmaple
Ottawa46 contributions
0
style over substance
Jan 2018 • Couples
We visited this restaurant because we'd be told it was the best place to experience "authentic" south Vietnamese dishes. The place is beautiful and the staff attentive, pleasant and efficient. Sadly, the place lacks warmth or true character and the focus seems to be on how the food is presented more than the food itself. Rice is cooked in clay bowls which are tossed in the air several times when ready, then the bowl is smashed and the rice, which retains the shape of the bowl, is tossed from one end of the room to the other where it is caught by a waiter or a selected patron. Wonderful to see once or twice during a meal but boring and intrusive when done to such excess. The staff almost demands everyone pay attention, I was even called out by a waiter for not interrupting my conversation with my wife to watch yet another rice toss. Apparently he wasn't aware this was supposed to be a restaurant not an interactive dinner theatre. This dropped the service rating from a 5 to a 3. Overall I found the restaurant to be over priced and pretentious. Unless you're nervous about eating in anything less than an upscale restaurant, or one trying to be, there are far better places to enjoy an "authentic" meal.
